behavior: dotf mem session-end archives the MEMORY.md `## Session Handoff` block into 10_projects/<project>/sessions/<date>-<project>-claude.md, and is a resilient no-op on every trivial/missing/malformed input
The `dotf mem session-end` command reads the SessionEnd payload on stdin and always exits 0 (never crashes a session), even on malformed input
The session-handoff.{sh,ps1} twins are deleted and the SessionEnd hook is wired directly to dotf mem session-end (no shim); a guard pins no regression

dotf mem session-start emits the agnostic session-brief byte-equivalent to scripts/session-brief.sh across representative CWDs and both --format values (POSIX gate; the Windows .ps1 equivalence lands in PR2b)
The sb_* emitters (vault detect/health/specs/lessons/baseline) and the --format=stdout|markdown runner are ported faithfully, preserving the leading-blank framing and exact message text

The OS-agnostic memlink primitive links an agent's per-project memory dir to its vault source (symlink on POSIX, directory junction on Windows), idempotently and best-effort, converging ensure-memory-symlink.sh and the Windows junction hook; source resolution honours the three vault conventions

The Claude session-start injectors (SDD-004 config reader, claude.json-size, knowledge-health, memory-temperature, doctor-drift, hive/work-SDK detect, auto-memory link) each produce their exact CONTEXT_LINES contribution, ported byte-equivalent from claude-session-start.sh

dotf mem session-start (no --format) is the Claude SessionStart hook: it assembles the agnostic brief + Claude injectors in claude-session-start.sh's exact CONTEXT_LINES order and emits the additionalContext JSON envelope, byte-equivalent to the shell hook (golden-fixture gated; jq-equivalent encoding with ordered keys and no HTML escaping)
